claim: The LMAO stored-program loader image has 18,740 bytes of headroom and admits
both 512 extra data cells and 8 new code flags, so the unified image (b) is
not blocked by the LMAO initializer budget on the loader side. The wall that
E3 and the extensibility probe measured belongs to the arithmetic and
comparator images, not to the loader.

artifact.demonstrated: loads prog_0..3 into RAM and runs them by PC, 4/4 (mbir_m2_loader_smoke.json)

method.description: Same probe shape as e3_lmao_initializer_budget.json and
cmp_lt_extensibility_probe.json, but applied to the loader image,
which has twelve times the headroom of the comparator image.
method.control: the untouched mbir_m2_loader.hell assembles to 40,309 bytes

comparison_with_other_images: mbir_alu.hell (54,691 B, headroom 4,358): 2 flags OK, 4 flags FAIL (e3).
mbir_cmp_lt.hell (57,511 B, headroom 1,538): even 1 new flag FAILS, data cells fail non-monotonically (cmp_lt_extensibility_probe).
mbir_m2_loader.hell (40,309 B, headroom 18,740): 512 data cells OK, 8 new flags OK.
consequence_for_b: The unified image's obstacle is NOT the LMAO initializer budget on the loader side: the loader admits the flags and data cells the arithmetic routes need.
The previously measured walls belong to the images one would have to EXTEND: the streaming ALU image (4,358 B headroom) and the comparator image (1,538 B headroom). The loader is the one with room.
So (b) reduces to writing the merged kernel on the loader's andamio, not to a budget fight. That is engineering work, and this measurement removes the 'it cannot fit' objection.
what_this_does_not_demonstrate: That the merged kernel actually fits: only the flag/cell dimensions were probed, and the arithmetic handler code itself was not added.
That the merged image runs correctly.
Anything about the native-emitter loader limit measured in native_probe_d.json, which is a separate and still valid finding.
scope_limits: Measured on mbir_m2_loader.hell with the same flag/cell shape as the other probes.
